title: SLO Change Experiment Lab and Rollback Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a repeatable, low-risk process for running controlled SLO change experiments (tweaks to target/weighting/counting rules) across Redwood Inference services. It covers experiment design, telemetry and gating, phased traffic rollout, capacity hedging, automated rollback triggers, and post-experiment acceptance criteria. The goal is to gather high-confidence signals about customer-visible impact before committing SLO changes company-wide.

Scope
-----
Applies to: inference-gateway, realtime-api, batcher, embed-service, and colocated model-serving nodes.
Not in scope: platform billing SLOs and external partner SLAs; those follow the contracts team process.

When to use this lab
--------------------
- Changing a latency SLO (e.g., P95 target from 150ms -> 120ms)
- Changing error-budget counting rules (e.g., transition from 4xx+5xx to 5xx-only)
- Adjusting SLO weights for multi-tenant teams
- Testing new fallback or degradation behaviors that affect SLOs

Prerequisites
-------------
1) Service owners identified and on-call covered for experiment window.
2) Active synthetic canaries for the SLO (canary-suite: inference-p95, embed-throughput).
3) Observability deck updated: dashboards, SLO pulse, burn-rate alerting, and latency drill-downs.
4) Capacity hedges defined (cold warm pools, burst absorber, pre-provisioned nodes).
5) Runbook notified channel: #sre-experiments and SLO-experiments-calendar entry.

Roles & ownership
------------------
- Experiment Owner: leads plan, run, and postmortem. (Example: Priya Nair)
- Service Owner: responsible for service-level mitigations and logs. (Example: Miguel Ramos - inference-gateway)
- Observability Engineer: ensures SLO metrics and burn-rate are instrumented and actionable.
- SRE Safety Lead: authority to abort experiments if safety gates trip.

Designing the experiment
------------------------
1) Define the hypothesis in a single sentence. Example: "Reducing P95 SLO target from 150ms to 130ms for realtime-api will not increase 5xx error-rate beyond 0.3% at 5% traffic with current autoscale policy."
2) Define measurable metrics (primary/secondary):
   - Primary: SLO burn rate over 30m windows; P95 latency for realtime-api.
   - Secondary: 5xx rate, tail memory OOM count, cache miss-rate, customer-perceived error rate (sampled tokens).
3) Define pass/fail criteria:
   - Pass if burn rate <= 1.0 for the experiment cohort over 2 hours and 5xx rate delta < 0.1 percentage points versus baseline.
   - Fail if burn rate >= 2.0 sustained for 15 minutes or 5xx rate delta >= 0.5 percentage points.
4) Define traffic cohorts and length (see Traffic Phases table).

Traffic Phases (example)
------------------------
Phase | Cohort % | Duration | Objective
------|----------|----------|---------
Baseline | 0% | 30m | Capture pre-change baseline metrics
Canary | 2% | 30m | Smoke test correctness under small load
Ramp1 | 5% | 1h | Validate metrics and capacity hedges
Ramp2 | 15% | 2h | Evaluate tail effects and cross-tenant interactions
Full | 100% (optional) | 24h | Only for green experiments and product approval

Telemetry & gating
------------------
- SLO burn-rate alerting: configured at three severity levels
  - advisory: burn_rate >= 0.8 (informational)
  - action: burn_rate >= 1.5 for 10m (auto-scaling/traffic-hold)
  - abort: burn_rate >= 2.0 for 15m (automated rollback)
- Error-rate gates: abort if 5xx_rate_delta >= 0.5
- System health gates: OOM_count > 0 or CPU_util increase > 40% sustained -> abort
- Evidence capture: all gates must log to experiment run id and attach traces for the first 200 failing requests

Automated controls (operational tooling)
---------------------------------------
We use two automation primitives integrated into the experiment pipeline:
1) Traffic controller (redwood-experiments) - adjusts route weights and records cohort id.
2) Safety orchestrator (sre-safety) - subscribes to burn-rate alerts and executes rollback when abort criteria are met.

CLI examples
------------
# Create experiment:
redwood-experiments create --service realtime-api --change '{"slo.p95_target_ms":130}' --owner priya.nair --id re-slo-exp-2026-06
# Ramp to 5%:
redwood-experiments set-weight --id re-slo-exp-2026-06 --cohort canary --weight 0.05
# Abort (manual):
redwood-experiments abort --id re-slo-exp-2026-06 --reason "observed burn-rate spike"

Runbook: Execute the SLO change experiment (step-by-step)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-run checklist (T-48h):
   - Notify stakeholders and schedule calendar entry.
   - Verify canaries synthetic-suite health (green for 24h).
   - Ensure capacity hedges are warm: 10% warm pool pre-provisioned for realtime-api.
2) Create experiment record in experiments tracker and attach plan.
3) Baseline capture (30m): record metrics and snapshot autoscale state.
4) Apply single-node config change behind feature-flag where possible (dry run).
5) Canary (2%): monitor burn-rate, errors, traces. If advisory alerts fire, investigate but continue.
6) Ramp1 (5%): after 30m stable, increase to 5%; run two targeted load patterns (short tail-heavy and long streaming).
7) Ramp2 (15%): validate cross-tenant interference and KV cache hit behavior.
8) Decision point: if pass criteria are met, continue to product signoff; if abort criteria met, trigger automated rollback and follow the incident review path.

Rollback procedure (automated + manual)
--------------------------------------
Automated rollback (preferred):
- Trigger: abort gate hit (see Telemetry & gating).
- Action: safety orchestrator invokes redwood-experiments abort, reverts traffic weights to pre-experiment snapshot, and signals autoscaler to return to baseline pools.
- Notifications: page SRE Safety Lead, post message to #sre-incidents, create incident record with tag experiment-id.

Manual rollback (when automation unavailable):
1) Service owner runs: redwood-experiments abort --id <exp-id> --reason "manual abort"
2) Revert config in config-store: git revert <commit> && deploy revert with canary cadence.
3) If stateful change (cache or schema), run recovery migration steps documented in service runbook.

Post-experiment: acceptance criteria & postmortem
------------------------------------------------
- Acceptance checklist (to be executed within 24h of experiment end):
  - Verify all cohorts returned to nominal traffic weights.
  - Confirm no residual elevated error-rates in last 72h.
  - Synthetic canaries back to green for 24h.
  - Runbook: document observed deltas and instrumentation gaps.
- Postmortem (for fails or unexpected impacts):
  - 3-day postmortem draft, include evidence links, raw traces, and the experiment run id.
  - Identify mitigation changes (config, autoscale thresholds, cache sizing).
  - Define follow-up experiments if hypothesis inconclusive.

Capacity planning & hedging guidance
-----------------------------------
- Reserve a minimum warm-pool equal to 10% of 99th percentile concurrency for the service being experimented on.
- Maintain a burst absorber pool (shared across model-serving) sized to absorb 2x normal short-term burst for up to 30m.
- Update capacity playbook entries when experiment shows systematic headroom change > 15%.

Template: experiment metadata (YAML)
----------------------------------
experiment_id: re-slo-exp-2026-06
service: realtime-api
change_summary: "p95 target 150->130 ms; counting rule unchanged"
hypothesis: "No material increase in 5xx or burn rate at 5% traffic"
owner: priya.nair@redwood.ai
start_window: "2026-06-18T14:00:00Z"
phases:
  - {name: baseline, pct: 0, duration_min: 30}
  - {name: canary, pct: 2, duration_min: 30}
  - {name: ramp1, pct: 5, duration_min: 60}
  - {name: ramp2, pct: 15, duration_min: 120}
abort_criteria:
  - "burn_rate >= 2.0 for 15m"
  - "5xx_rate_delta >= 0.5"

Evidence & artifacts to collect
-------------------------------
- Experiment manifest and config snapshots (git commit ids).
- Synthetic canary traces and raw request samples for first 200 failures.
- Autoscaler events and node provisioning timelines.
- Queryable SLO burn logs and alert history.

Acceptance decision matrix (quick)
---------------------------------
- Green: pass criteria met -> product review -> schedule rollout (gradual)
- Yellow: partial signals or instrumentation gaps -> design follow-up test -> re-run after fixes
- Red: abort criteria or other regressions -> rollback, full postmortem, capacity remediation
